scope: Targeted third-round GitHub candidates for ACR106 (trace/resume), ACR008 (cache identity), ACR009 (retry_policy + multiple subgraphs), ACR010 (conditional self-loop writing non-reducer keys).
method: gh api search/issues with 4 target keyword groups (59 queries); bodies+comments fetched for 68 issue/PR candidates; gist links inspected for trace content. Collection stopped on lead instruction before further expansion.

ACR106.explanation: 5 issues carry real debug/astream_events sequences (3875, 4217, 2942, 5764, 4985); 3875 and 4217 include resume markers. None shows a node that had completed before the resume marker starting again, so no ACR106 positive. 3875/4217 are negative controls, 2942/5764/4985 exercise trace parsing. 3 further symptom-relevant issues (6792, 7361, 7417) have no trace.

ACR008.explanation: The exact callable-identity/__dynamic__ failure case (#8753) is in the excluded first batch, so it cannot be reused. 7 new issues are cache-identity/namespace adjacent (key-encoding collision, cache vs checkpointer, stale cache key identity, namespace scoping) and are labelled match_level=adjacent; they do not validate the exact ACR008 claim.

ACR009.explanation: No new independent sample of 'node with retry_policy invoking 2+ subgraphs' was found in the downloaded material. The only exact hits (#9253, the issue) and its fix PR #9279 are the excluded first-batch case, so they are intentionally not counted. Near misses (#1618 Send-to-subgraph checkpoint id, #6864 checkpoint_ns numeric segments) do not have retry_policy in a node with multiple subgraph invokes.

ACR010.explanation: No new sample of a conditional self-loop writing a declared non-reducer key was found (#2336 is excluded). Keyword hits were loops around interrupt() (#9001, #3275), fan-in issues (#142), or template format errors (#1565), none matching the conditional self-loop + non-reducer write structure.

candidates.title: Bug: Error when having multiple nodes, each with a single `interrupt`
candidates.summary: Bug report with a full stream_mode="debug" event log across an interrupt and a Command(resume="continue") run on the same thread: checkpoint -> task(branch_1/branch_2) -> task_result(branch_1, interrupts during); after the resume marker the same two tasks start again and branch_1 fails with ValueError('list.remove(x): x not in list').
candidates.notes: Trace source: issue body (two debug-stream blocks separated by 'Interrupted! Continuing...'). Resume marker present. The re-started nodes were interrupted (task_result carries interrupts during), not completed before resume, so this trace does NOT prove the ACR106 symptom; useful as a resume-trace parser case / negative control.

candidates.title: create_react_agent fails to resume after external update_state with ToolMessage (tried with astream/ainvoke)
candidates.summary: create_react_agent thread updated externally with update_state; resumption via astream(None, stream_mode="debug") yields only one checkpoint debug chunk (values contain the externally added ToolMessage, next=[]), and no node re-executes.
candidates.notes: Trace source: issue body, explicit 'ATTEMPTING RESUMPTION ... Received DEBUG chunk after resume' log with a real debug event. Resume-marked trace, but it shows a no-op resume (no node re-run), so not an ACR106 positive; candidate for trace parsing / control.

candidates.title: When I use interrupt and astream_events, the error RuntimeError: Called get_configurable outside of a runnable context occurs
candidates.summary: interrupt() plus astream_events(version="v2") raises RuntimeError: Called get_configurable; the body pastes a long ordered astream_events sequence (on_chain_start/end, tool_call, function events carrying langgraph_step/langgraph_node/checkpoint metadata).
candidates.notes: Trace source: issue body. Real astream_events sequence, but no resume/replay marker and no evidence of a completed node restarting -> not an ACR106 positive; still usable to test event-sequence parsing.

candidates.title: Bug: `task_result` events with errors are not yielded when streaming in `stream_mode="debug"`
candidates.summary: stream_mode="debug" drops task_result events that carry an error; body pastes real debug events for node 'failer' (type task, then expected task_result) showing the missing error event.
candidates.notes: Trace source: issue body ('STREAM EVENT: {...}' debug chunks). Real debug event sequence, no resume/replay; not an ACR106 positive.

candidates.title: get_state values is not updated  in stream_mode="values". Reproducible rate 1/10.
candidates.summary: stream_mode="values" sometimes leaves get_state stale; a comment pastes debug-mode output (task_result for step_0, then checkpoint/task step_1) showing the task_result not reflected in the snapshot.
candidates.notes: Trace source: issue comment by reporter ('Additional information I tried in debug mode'). Real debug events with step/payload; no resume/replay marker; not an ACR106 positive.

candidates.title: Resuming after interrupt doesn't reuse prior task outputs when interrupt is in subgraph
candidates.summary: Resuming an interrupt that sits inside a subgraph does not reuse prior task outputs and re-executes node work; no debug trace/event sequence pasted.
candidates.notes: Symptom-relevant to ACR106 (resume re-execution) but has_trace=false; material is code + state snapshots, so it cannot serve as an ACR106 trace sample.

candidates.title: When resume from a specific checkpoint_id, it becomes replay
candidates.summary: Resuming from a specific checkpoint_id behaves like a replay: the second run re-executes from the beginning instead of continuing at the interrupt.
candidates.notes: Symptom-relevant replay case, but no pasted debug trace/events -> has_trace=false; cannot validate ACR106.

candidates.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
candidates.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls taking ~180s+ are silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original still runs (2-3x duplicated work); 86-comment thread.
candidates.notes: Strongest real-world symptom of resume/checkpoint re-execution, but no trace/event log and no repro code (linked gists are SQLite dedup patterns, not traces) -> has_trace=false; not usable as ACR106 trace sample.

candidates.title: RedisCache key encoding collides when namespace or cache key contains ':'
candidates.summary: RedisCache._make_key flattens a namespace tuple and the cache key into one colon-delimited string, so distinct FullKey values collide when a namespace segment or key contains ':' and a cache hit can return another namespace's value.
candidates.notes: Adjacent cache-identity case (key encoding not injective). Not the callable-identity/__dynamic__ mechanism of ACR008, but exercises cross-namespace wrong-hit; code in body.

candidates.title: LangGraph Caching Issue with Pydantic Models
candidates.summary: Caching with CachePolicy() is inconsistent when the graph state is a Pydantic model: logically identical states serialize non-deterministically, so cache hits/misses depend on serialization rather than on identity.
candidates.notes: Adjacent: cache key identity depends on state serialization, not callable identity; still a real wrong-cache-hit class.

candidates.title: In memory cache doesn't work with in memory checkpointer
candidates.summary: Adding InMemorySaver to a graph that uses InMemoryCache makes the cache stop working (cache and checkpointer interaction).
candidates.notes: Adjacent: shared cache across the same graph with a checkpointer; not callable identity.

candidates.title: Caching does not take function code into consideration
candidates.summary: Cache key ignores the function body/code, so changing a node implementation still returns cached results from the old implementation.
candidates.notes: Adjacent: 'identity of the cached callable' is missing (code version), not module/qualname collapse; no reproducible code block in issue body.

candidates.title: When langgraph's stream_mode includes custom, the cached results do not contain custom data.
candidates.summary: When stream_mode includes 'custom', cached results do not contain custom data that the uncached node emits, so cache hit changes observable output.
candidates.notes: Adjacent: cache hit/identity affects emitted custom data; not callable identity.

candidates.title: Functional API with a cache: concurrent nested tasks fail with "dictionary changed size during iteration" in `match_cached_writes`
candidates.summary: Functional API with a cache: parallel nested tasks fail with RuntimeError 'dictionary changed size during iteration' in match_cached_writes (task registration vs cache matching without a lock).
candidates.notes: Adjacent: cache matching/identity in parallel tasks; real error, but root cause is concurrency, not callable identity.

candidates.title: RedisCache.clear([()]) deletes every cache namespace instead of only the empty namespace
candidates.summary: RedisCache.clear([()]) deletes every cache namespace instead of only the empty namespace, so clearing one cache scope clears unrelated scopes.
candidates.notes: Adjacent: cache namespace identity/scoping; not callable identity. Included as a namespace-handling case only.
